name: room
text: Room opened — goal: memory: Recall by meaning, relate elements, build the brain graph, embed unembedded elements.

name: Graft
text:
Do this: Build a single, shared memory graph that links every idea across all conversations and tools. Every new memory gets tagged with its meaning and connected to existing nodes by how it relates—so recall isn’t just keyword search, it’s mental retrieval.

Trade-off: We lose speed today to save time forever. Manual tagging and linking slows down writing, but it turns memory from a dump into a brain that grows with us.

name: Prune
text: The real risk isn’t speed—it’s that forcing a single graph upfront will lock us into brittle connections before we even know what we need to remember. A better alternative is to let the graph emerge naturally from repeated use, tagging only what proves critical, and pruning the rest. Settle it by running a two-week experiment: track how often we actually need mental retrieval versus keyword search, then decide.
